title: Native Sieve interpreter: replace sieve-rs with MIT crate
description:
Write a minimal MIT-licensed Sieve interpreter covering RFC 5228 core + RFC 5229 variables, replacing the AGPL sieve-rs dependency entirely. No daemon, no IPC.

Why this issue exists:
usenet-ipfs-smtp is AGPL because it links sieve-rs (AGPL-3.0-only). Writing a focused native implementation covering only what the project needs produces a MIT crate, drops the AGPL entirely, and removes the daemon architecture.

Sieve (RFC 5228) is a restricted filtering language: no loops, no user-defined functions, fixed command and test sets. The subset needed is:
  Commands: require, if/elsif/else, stop, fileinto, reject, discard, keep, set (RFC 5229)
  Tests: header, address, envelope, exists, size, allof, anyof, not, true, false
  Comparators/match: :is :contains :matches, :comparator, i;ascii-casemap i;octet
  Address parts: :localpart :domain :all
  Variables (RFC 5229): set, ${var} substitution

Total implementation: ~1250 lines in one crate, zero new deps.

What needs to be done:
- crates/sieve-native: new MIT crate, same public API as current usenet-ipfs-sieve (compile/evaluate/SieveAction/CompiledScript)
- Lexer + parser producing a typed AST
- Evaluator walking the AST against a raw RFC 5322 message
- Variables extension
- Test suite cross-validating against sieve-rs (dev-dep oracle)
- Wire into smtp: drop usenet-ipfs-sieve, change smtp license to MIT, remove AGPL from workspace
